chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q2 Quantitative Analysis (4 points) — Set 1: climate-change opinion line graph
chunks.content: AP Government FRQ 2 is Quantitative Analysis, 4 points, one per part A/B/C/D, based on a data graphic. Task pattern: A identify a specific data value, B describe a trend/pattern in the data, C draw a conclusion linking the data to a political actor/institution (e.g., how an interest group could use a trend), D explain how the data/trend relates to a course concept (e.g., political ideology, participation). Set 1 answer key: A [1] identify the 2010 percentage from the line graph; B [1] describe a trend in the line graph; C [1] draw a conclusion about how an interest group could use a trend; D [1] explain how the overall trend could result from a course concept (e.g., political socialization/ideology). Common failure: for B, restating one value instead of a trend; for D, describing the trend again rather than explaining a cause.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 4/4 — identified the 2010 value (A), described a valid trend (B), drew a conclusion about interest-group use of a trend (C), and explained a course-concept cause of the trend (D). Full-credit model for Quantitative Analysis.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2B, 3/4
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 3/4 — earned the data identification, trend description, and conclusion, but lost one part, typically D (explained by restating the trend rather than giving a course-concept cause). Illustrates the common miss on the final explain point.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q2 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 2C, 2/4
chunks.content: Q2 (Set 1) scored 2/4 — earned the data identification and trend description (A, B) but lost the conclusion (C) and the explanation (D). Illustrates a response that reads the graph but cannot connect the data to political actors or concepts.
